scenes.text: Halloween is secretly an astronomy holiday.
It's a cross-quarter day, roughly halfway between the autumn equinox and the winter solstice.
The ancient Celts celebrated it as Samhain, which means summer's end.
For them, it was also New Year's Eve, the start of the dark half of the year.
The true astronomical midpoint actually lands in early November, but the date stuck at October thirty-first.
Groundhog Day, May Day and Lammas are the other three cross-quarter days.
Did you know Halloween had roots in the sky?

title: Halloween is secretly an astronomy holiday 🎃
caption: Halloween is a cross-quarter day, roughly midway between the autumn equinox and winter solstice. The Celts marked it as Samhain, "summer's end" and their new year. 🎃
